Your new role     Joining Hays, means you'll be part of a forward-thinking business that's going places. Our global network and ways of working mean you'll be part of something bigger, whilst taking pride in the work you do within a collaborative team.    We are currently looking for a Senior Manager/Bids Director to join our Hays team with preference to be based in our Hays Sydney CBD office or any of our eastern seaboard offices. In this role, you will be responsible for providing senior leadership and strategic direction of the bids function, accountable for the governance, quality and the delivery of complex, high value tenders and bids. Moorookclub Pty Ltd operates Blanchetown Foodery, a vibrant one-stop destination in the heart of Blanchetown, South Australia, encompassing a cafe, restaurant, and supermarket. The business specialises in delivering a diverse multi-cuisine experience, featuring Italian, Indian, and fast-food options alongside everyday grocery needs. Known for its convenient, high-quality offerings and friendly service in a regional community setting, Blanchetown Foodery values fresh ingredients, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence. It fosters a supportive, team-oriented workplace culture where dedication to food service and community connection are highly regarded.
About the Position:
The Chef plays a central role at Blanchetown Foodery within Moorookclub Pty Ltd, leading the preparation and delivery of high-quality dishes across the cafe and restaurant operations. This position involves creating appealing menus, maintaining exceptional food standards, and contributing to the smooth running of a busy multi-cuisine venue that serves both locals and visitors. The role is essential for upholding the business’s reputation for delicious, diverse food and ensuring an outstanding dining experience that supports the venue’s position as a community favourite.

Planning menus, estimating food and labour costs, and ordering food supplies.
Monitoring quality of dishes at all stages of preparation and presentation.
Discussing food preparation issues with Managers, Dietitians and kitchen and waiting staff.
Demonstrating techniques and advising on cooking procedures.
Preparing and cooking food.
Explaining and enforcing hygiene regulations.
Selecting and training staff (as required).
Freezing and preserving foods (as required).
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Diploma in a relevant field (such as Commercial Cookery or Hospitality Management).
Minimum 3 years’ work experience as a Chef.
Strong technical skills in multi-cuisine food preparation (including Italian, Indian, and fast food), menu planning, cost control, and presentation.
Excellent knowledge of food safety, hygiene regulations, and quality standards.
Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and provide guidance to kitchen staff.
Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced setting while maintaining attention to detail.

Job Title	 Chef/Chef De Partie
Salary range	 $79,500 - $90,000 + Superannuation – depending on skill level
Job Closure date	 30 days

About Our Client
Our client is an award-winning luxury hotel, renowned as a vibrant landmark where modern sophistication meets unparalleled service. They are celebrated for creating immersive, memorable experiences for their guests, from the elegance of their accommodations to the dynamic energy of their world-class dining and entertainment precinct. The culinary philosophy is centred on contemporary, produce-driven cuisine, showcasing the finest local and seasonal ingredients with artistry and precision. They are seeking a passionate and skilled Chef de Partie to join their exceptional culinary brigade.

About the Role
We are recruiting on behalf of our client for a dedicated Chef de Partie to become an integral part of their high-energy kitchen team. This is not just a job; it's an opportunity to contribute to a culinary landscape known for its innovation and excellence. You will be responsible for managing a specific section of the kitchen, ensuring every dish that leaves your station meets the impeccable standards expected by their discerning guests. You will play a key role in bringing their celebrated menus to life, working with premium ingredients in a fast-paced, professional, and collaborative environment.

Key Responsibilities & Duties
Menu Development & Kitchen Management
• Collaborate with the Senior Chef team in the creative process of researching, developing, and costing new menu items that align with the hotel's contemporary and seasonal culinary direction.
• Manage the efficient ordering and organisation of high-quality food supplies for your section, minimising waste while maintaining the highest standards of ingredient quality.
• Assist in calculating detailed food and labour costs for your designated kitchen section to ensure financial targets and budgetary guidelines are consistently met.

Culinary Execution & Quality Control
• Expertly prepare, cook, and present a diverse range of dishes to the exact specification of the Head Chef, demonstrating advanced technical skills and a keen eye for detail.
• Meticulously monitor the quality, flavour, and visual presentation of all dishes at every stage, from initial mise en place to final plating, ensuring consistency and excellence.
• Take ownership of your section during service periods, demonstrating leadership, organisation, and the ability to perform under pressure to deliver a seamless dining experience.

Leadership, Training & Hygiene Standards
• Proactively participate in the training and development of Commis Chefs and apprentices, mentoring them in classic and modern cooking techniques and procedures.
• Uphold and rigorously enforce the company’s comprehensive health, safety, and hygiene regulations, including HACCP protocols, to ensure a pristine and safe working environment at all times.
• Foster clear and effective communication by discussing daily preparation, potential challenges, and special dietary requirements with Managers, Sous Chefs, and service staff.

Candidate Profile & Requirements
• Proven experience as a Chef de Partie or Demi Chef de Partie within a high-volume, à la carte or fine-dining kitchen environment.
• A formal qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or equivalent) is highly regarded.
• A genuine passion for contemporary, produce-driven cuisine and a commitment to culinary excellence.
• Demonstrated ability to manage a section, lead by example, and support junior team members.
• Comprehensive knowledge of kitchen operations, including but not limited to butchery, seafood preparation, and sauce work.
• An unwavering commitment to maintaining the highest standards of cleanliness and food safety.
• Excellent communication skills, a positive and collaborative team spirit, and the ability to thrive in a demanding, fast-paced environment.
• Flexibility to work across a rotating roster, including evenings, weekends, and public holidays.

To Apply
If you are a culinary professional ready to take the next step in your career within a celebrated and dynamic hotel environment, we would like to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a cover letter detailing your relevant experience via the link below.

Full time positions available with projects located across New South Wales.

This role requires a strong leader who can lead and manage rope access construction teams while ensuring safety, productivity, and quality standards are consistently met.

* Conduct pre-starts, toolbox talks, and safety briefings
* Complete daily reports, safety documentation, and permit systems

* Oversee installation of ground support systems including rock bolts, mesh, and shotcrete preparation
* Monitor work quality and productivity of rope access teams

Required Qualifications & Experience

* IRATA Rope Access Certification (preferred)
* White card

* Minimum 3 years experience in ground engineering / civil infrastructure
* Demonstrated experience supervising rope access teams
* Experience in slope stabilization, scaling, rock bolting, or geotechnical works
* Previous mining site experience strongly preferred
* Strong knowledge of rope access safety procedures and risk management

Key Attributes

* Strong leadership and communication skills
* Safety-focused mindset

result.description:
Join this government agency that is looking for an immediately available EL1 Communication Manager.   Your new company  Join a Government organisation that supports services to a nationally significant workforce. This organisation is committed to delivering high-quality services, maintaining strong stakeholder relationships, and driving strategic communication outcomes across a diverse operational environment.   Your new role  
 As the Communication Manager, you'll act as the trusted communications adviser for a portfolio of business areas, partnering directly with senior executives to plan and deliver high-impact communication strategies and products. 
 Working across both internal and external communications, you'll take ownership of communication planning, executive messaging, issues management and digital content delivery. You'll be responsible for translating complex operational information into clear, engaging content and ensuring messaging is consistent across multiple channels and audiences. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Leading end-to-end communication strategies for major business initiatives and organisational priorities. 
 Providing high-level advice to senior executives on communication risks, opportunities and stakeholder engagement approaches. 
 Developing executive briefs, key messages, communication plans, web content, articles, speeches and organisational announcements. 
 Managing digital publishing and content governance processes, ensuring compliance with government accessibility and digital standards. 
 Monitoring communication performance and providing insights and recommendations to improve engagement outcomes. 
 Managing, leading and mentoring a small team. 
 
  What you'll need to succeed  
 
 Baseline security clearance is required. 
 Significant experience delivering strategic communications within government, corporate or highly regulated environments. 
 Demonstrated success developing communication plans, executive messaging and stakeholder engagement strategies for complex projects or organisational change initiatives. 
 Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to quickly distil technical or policy-heavy information into clear, audience-focused content. 
 Strong experience managing website content, digital publishing workflows and content governance processes. 
 The confidence to influence senior stakeholders and provide trusted communications advice in a fast-moving environment. 
 Experience balancing multiple priorities while managing competing deadlines and responding to emerging issues. 
 Familiarity with platforms such as GovCMS or similar enterprise content management systems will be highly regarded. 
 
  What you'll get in return  
 
 Attractive EL1-equivalent hourly rate. 
 Immediate start contract with the potential to contribute to several high-profile communication initiatives. 
 North Canberra-based opportunity with flexible working arrangements available in line with business requirements. 
 Opportunity to work directly with senior leaders and influence organisational communication outcomes. 
 A supportive and collaborative communications team that values innovation, initiative and continuous improvement. 
 
  What you need to do now   If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.    Please note, due to the nature of the role, we are currently seeking candidates based locally. Interstate applicants are kindly asked not to apply at this time.   Michelle Liv    Senior Business Manager Marketing & Communications HAYS    T: 02 6112 7653    E:  michelle.liv@hays.com.au      Please  click here  to apply.

result.description:
Rix Asset Maintenance is seeking experienced Site Supervisors to join our team in QLD, supporting a number of slope stabilization projects across the civil, mining and infrastructure sectors throughout Queensland.

Full time positions available with projects located across Queensland.

About the Role

As the Site Supervisor, you will oversee all aspects of geotechnical stabilization works including various Drilling operations, Anchor installation, Grouting, Anchor testing, Rock fall netting and catch fence installation, Steel fixing, Formwork, Concrete, Shotcrete, and Scaling.

This role requires a strong leader who can lead and manage rope access construction teams while ensuring safety, productivity, and quality standards are consistently met.

Key Responsibilities

* Supervision and coordination of rope access crews including subcontractors, suppliers, plant and equipment
* Ensure that plant, equipment, staff and subcontractors operate within safe working conditions and ensure that all operations meet the environmental, safety and legislative requirements
* Conduct pre-starts, toolbox talks, and safety briefings
* Complete daily reports, safety documentation, and permit systems
* Conduct risk assessments, pre-work safety checks and equipment inspections while ensuring compliance is within industry standards
* Oversee installation of ground support systems including rock bolts, mesh, and shotcrete preparation
* Monitor work quality and productivity of rope access teams

Required Qualifications & Experience

* IRATA Rope Access Certification (preferred)
* White card
* Driving licence
* Minimum 3 years experience in ground engineering / civil infrastructure
* Demonstrated experience supervising rope access teams
* Experience in slope stabilisation, scaling, rock bolting, or geotechnical works
* Previous mining site experience strongly preferred
* Strong knowledge of rope access safety procedures and risk management

Key Attributes

* Strong leadership and communication skills
* Safety-focused mindset

result.description:
Pressure Welder (ANZSCO 322312)
Employer: C&J Fabrications
Location: Nowra, NSW, Australia
Employment Type: Full-Time Permanent
Salary: $80,000 - $85,000

Job Ad Start Date: 10/07/26
Job Ad Finish Date: 09/08/26

About the Role:
C&J Fabrications is seeking a qualified and experienced Pressure Welder to join our fabrication and manufacturing operations in Australia. The successful candidate will perform high-quality pressure welding on pipes, vessels, structural components, and heavy fabrication equipment according to Australian Standards, engineering specifications, and workplace safety requirements. This role is crucial in supporting operational demands within the manufacturing and engineering sector, where suitably qualified Australian workers have not been available despite genuine recruitment efforts.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
- Perform pressure welding using MIG, TIG, FCAW, Stick, and other welding techniques.
- Weld pressure pipes, tanks, boilers, and structural steel components.
- Interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and welding procedures.
- Operate welding equipment and fabrication machinery safely and efficiently.
- Conduct weld preparation, grinding, gouging, cutting, and finishing.
- Inspect completed welds for structural integrity and quality compliance.
- Perform welding in accordance with AS/NZS welding standards and site specifications.
- Maintain workshop safety and comply with WHS requirements.
- Complete fabrication and repair work within project deadlines.
- Participate in shutdowns, maintenance projects, and site installations as required.

Minimum Requirements:

Qualifications:
- Relevant Trade Qualification equivalent to:
- Certificate III in Engineering – Fabrication Trade, or
- A recognized international welding trade qualification.
- Welding certifications are advantageous.

Experience:
- Minimum of 3 years of post-trade experience as a Pressure Welder.
- Experience in heavy fabrication, manufacturing, mining, oil & gas, or industrial environments is preferred.

Skills:
- Strong knowledge of pressure welding techniques.
- Ability to read and interpret technical drawings.
- Experience welding carbon steel, stainless steel, and alloy materials.
- Knowledge of Australian welding and safety standards.
- Strong problem-solving and communication skills.

result.description:
Working as a procurement & contracts specialist you will be responsible for providing end-to-end sourcing, contracting & contract administration across Tier 13 contractor packages & capital project procurement. During the planning pre-award phases, you will execute RFI/RFQ/RFP processes, manage prequalification and evaluation activities, lead commercial negotiations & prepare recommendations for award. You will draft, negotiate & execute contracts, statements of work & variations, while ensuring compliance with procurement policies and governance requirements. Your role will involve validating daily & weekly cost reporting (CWSR/CDSR), managing variations and emergent works, tracking KPIs  supporting corrective actions where required. You will maintain procurement dashboards, progress trackers & contribute to finance & project controls reporting. At close-out, you will support final invoicing, performance reviews, SAP close-out actions & ensure all records are archived in line with governance standards. The role requires close collaboration with senior procurement leaders, turnaround managers, HSE, legal, finance & external contractors to ensure safe & commercially sound project delivery. Min 5+ years experience in procurement & contract administration within turnarounds, shutdowns, mining, chemicals or heavy industry Proven end-to-end sourcing experience (RFI/RFQ/RFP), evaluation management & commercial negotiation
Strong contract drafting, execution & administration experience, including variations, emergent scope & KPI management
Experience working with SAP (P2P) & strong MS Office/Excel capability; Strong understanding of governance, procurement policies & compliance frameworks; Ability to manage multiple stakeholder relationships across HSE, IR/ER, Legal, Finance & Project Controls; Willingness to travel to Phosphate Hill & Mount Isa sites & work execution rosters, incl weekends where required
